paper_metadata.title: Quantum advantage of Monte Carlo option pricing

experiments.description: Noisy-simulation study of quantum-accelerated Monte Carlo option pricing for a European call option using the standard rescaling-based function application and quantum amplitude estimation, with optimization over qubit count, truncation, rescaling, and Grover schedule parameters.

algorithm.variant: Quantum-accelerated Monte Carlo (QAMC) with rescaling technique and QAE

hyperparameters.grover_schedule: exponentially increasing schedule with base 2; m0 = 0, mk = 2^(k-1) for k > 0

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The log-normal stock-price distribution is truncated to a finite interval and discretized into 2^n bins; probabilities are loaded into n state-preparation qubits. A comparator uses n ancilla qubits to mark S_i > K, and one payoff qubit stores the Bernoulli-encoded payoff.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate discounted expected payoff E[e^{-rT} max(S_T - K, 0)] under the Black-Scholes log-normal distribution.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Truncation of the distribution to [E[S_T] - w Var(S_T), E[S_T] + w Var(S_T)] and discretization into 2^n bins; rescaling approximation for the linear payoff region.

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing under the Black-Scholes-Merton model, evaluated on a grid of option parameters and qubit/noise settings.

dataset_specification.description: Black-Scholes log-normal distribution; parameter grid r in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2}, nu in {0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4}; at-the-money case S0 = K = 2; T = 1.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Truncate the distribution around the expectation by w standard-deviation units; discretize into 2^n bins; approximate the payoff linear part via rescaling.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical optimization over parameter grid; compare quantum and classical pricing errors; average quantum advantage over 11 options in one analysis; Nshot varied to satisfy relative error threshold.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: 2n + 1 total logical qubits; comparator requires n ancilla qubits; simulations explicitly shown for n = 3 (7 qubits total)

noise_model.noise_description: Depolarizing noise applied after every 1-qubit and 2-qubit gate except RZ; effective Grover-operator coherence probability fitted from simulation

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM native basis gates {CX, X, SX, RZ}
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Black-Scholes analytic distribution used to generate the discretized probability amplitudes; parameter sweep and numerical optimization over n, w, c, and schedule length.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Maximum-likelihood estimation of QAE probabilities; fit of effective coherence probability; compute quantum advantage metric and compare to classical Monte Carlo.

speedup_claims.conditions: ideal QAE/QAMC setting; error scaling O(1/N) versus classical O(1/sqrt(N))
speedup_claims.caveats: Systematic errors and hardware noise can eliminate the advantage; paper finds advantage only at very low CX error rates around 1e-6 to 1e-7.

speedup_claims.factor: about 20 logical qubits may be sufficient
speedup_claims.conditions: for European call option pricing under the tested parameter grid, with optimized parameters and low noise
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a simulation-based estimate, not hardware demonstration.

scalability_data.metric_value: optimized over n; best curve depends on noise level

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/N) estimation error for QAE; quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/sqrt(N)) estimation error for Monte Carlo
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: N = Nshot * Nq queries to A or A†; Nq = sum_k (2m_k + 1)
complexity_analysis.crossover_n: Quantum advantage observed only when CX error rate is around 1e-6 to 1e-7; about 20 logical qubits may be sufficient

experiments.description: Noisy-simulation study of the Fourier-series-based function application method for European call option pricing combined with quantum amplitude estimation, compared against the rescaling approach.

algorithm.variant: QAMC with Fourier-series-based function approximation and QAE

hyperparameters.grover_schedule: exponentially increasing schedule with base 2; m0 = 0, mk = 2^(k-1) for k > 0

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The discretized log-normal distribution is loaded into n qubits; the payoff is represented via multiple Fourier-term circuits using the comparator and linear-number-of-rotation-gates constructions.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate discounted expected payoff E[e^{-rT} max(S_T - K, 0)] using Fourier expansion of the payoff function.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Truncation/discretization of the distribution; smooth periodic continuation of the linear payoff part; truncation of the Fourier series at l_max.

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing under the Black-Scholes-Merton model, evaluated on the same option grid as the rescaling method.

dataset_specification.description: Black-Scholes log-normal distribution; parameter grid r in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2}, nu in {0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4}; at-the-money case S0 = K = 2; T = 1.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Truncate and discretize the distribution; choose x0 = K and xu = x_max - K to minimize the linear region; construct Fourier coefficients for the periodic continuation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical optimization over n, w, l_max, and schedule length; compare quantum advantage against classical Monte Carlo and against the rescaling technique; average over 11 options in one analysis.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: 2n + 1 total logical qubits; comparator requires n ancilla qubits; simulations explicitly shown for n = 3 (7 qubits total)

noise_model.noise_description: Depolarizing noise applied after every 1-qubit and 2-qubit gate except RZ; effective Grover-operator coherence probability fitted from simulation

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM native basis gates {CX, X, SX, RZ}
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Black-Scholes analytic distribution used to generate the discretized probability amplitudes; parameter sweep and numerical optimization over n, w, l_max, and schedule length.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Maximum-likelihood estimation of QAE probabilities; fit of effective coherence probability; compute quantum advantage metric and compare to classical Monte Carlo and rescaling baseline.

speedup_claims.factor: Fourier technique performs better across a wide range of CX errors
speedup_claims.baseline_method: rescaling technique and classical Monte Carlo
speedup_claims.conditions: tested on 11 options over r in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2} and nu in {0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4}
speedup_claims.caveats: Relative advantage is described as stable but exact numeric factor is not reported in text.

speedup_claims.conditions: ideal QAE scaling with Fourier-based function application
speedup_claims.caveats: Additional Fourier terms increase query cost; systematic errors still dominate at realistic noise levels.

scalability_data.metric_value: optimized over Fourier truncation; best performance in region l_max about 10 to 30

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/N) estimation error for QAE; quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo, but with extra queries scaling with l_max for Fourier terms
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/sqrt(N)) estimation error for Monte Carlo
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: Multiple amplitude-estimation tasks for Fourier coefficients; total queries increase by factor l_max^2 + 1 in the variance model
complexity_analysis.crossover_n: Quantum advantage observed only when CX error rate is around 1e-6 to 1e-7; Fourier method outperforms rescaling across a wide range of errors

experiments.description: Calibration experiment for the noisy amplitude-estimation model: fitting an effective Grover-operator coherence probability from gate-level depolarizing noise simulations, including a 2-qubit maximum-likelihood test and a 3-qubit coupling-map comparison.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Calibration of the QAE Grover operator acting on the option-pricing state-preparation and payoff circuit; no separate optimization problem beyond noise fitting.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Fit an effective coherence probability h_Theta to noisy measurement probabilities and compare against the Cramér-Rao lower bound / maximum-likelihood estimates.

problem_instance.description: Small calibration instances used to validate the noise model and finite-sample behavior of the estimator.

dataset_specification.description: 2-qubit case for maximum-likelihood finite-sample study; 3-qubit case for coupling-map/noise-model comparison in Figure A1.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Apply depolarizing noise after each gate; fit effective Grover coherence probability from simulated probabilities.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Maximum-likelihood simulations repeated 1000 times for each sample size; fit exponential correction to the ratio of realized standard deviation to the Cramér-Rao bound; compare all-to-all versus linear coupling.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: 2 qubits for ML calibration; 3 state-preparation qubits and 7 total qubits in the coupling-map comparison

noise_model.noise_description: Depolarizing channel on 1-qubit and 2-qubit gates; effective Grover-operator coherence probability fitted from noisy simulation

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM native basis gates {CX, X, SX, RZ}
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Fit likelihood model from simulated measurement probabilities; derive Cramér-Rao bound; exponential correction fit for finite-sample inefficiency.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Maximum-likelihood estimation repeated 1000 times; fit correction curve; compare coupling maps.

speedup_claims.caveats: This experiment calibrates the effective noise model rather than demonstrating algorithmic speedup.
